changes.text: The status stays complete, but the record's notes and its earlier change entry no longer say the paseo was built on the strength of the 2019 Phase 1 submittal, which was only a forecast. They now cite the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes (staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure, including the paseos around Building G) and the Port's June 2026 report (Phase 1 completed in 2025; the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure); neither names this paseo individually. The Port's Oct 2023 report is now cited for Parcel A being The Canyon and Parcel G's Visa work. The Jan 30, 2018 Design Controls approval milestone now cites the Sept 2019 Port memo that states the date, and notes that the memo numbers that resolution 18-05 while the January 26 staff report requested it as 18-04.

record.notes: Shared Public Way paseo (Dr Maya Angelou Lane, north segment) -- the pedestrian paseo between Block A/The Canyon and Block G/Visa, from Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) to China Basin Park; Design Controls Figure 3.1.1 marks it as Paseo 4.2. Built with Phase 1, per Port records of its acceptance: the 2019 Phase 1 submittal only planned it ('A pedestrian paseo in between Parcels A and G' among the public spaces that 'will be created as part of Phase 1'), but the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes record staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure and describe 'the paseos in the bottom around Building G leading in to China Basin Park' as Port owned (Resolutions 25-05, 25-06), and the Port's June 5, 2026 report says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and 'The City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure'. None of these names this paseo on its own. Parcel A as The Canyon is stated in the Port's Oct 2023 report and Parcel G as Visa's building in its Table 2. Its own real Assessor lot, 8719B001 (1,145 m2, recorded 2020-06-12); DataSF's street centerline names it Dr Maya Angelou Ln (CNN 15286000, layer PRIVATE). Added 2026-09-17.
